reason: This passage (Exodus 1-7) focuses primarily on the liberation of Israel from Egyptian slavery and God's covenant promises to the patriarchs. The central themes are redemption through divine power, the establishment of covenant relationship, and God's authority demonstrated through the plagues. While the text mentions God establishing a covenant and taking Israel as His people, it contains no explicit discussion of proper worship, sacrifices, offerings, cultic practices, or temple rituals. The statement reflects concerns central to Leviticus and other parts of the Torah, but not to this particular passage's narrative arc and theological emphasis.
